sections.overview: The lesser prairie-chicken is a grouse native to the southern and central High Plains of the United States.
sections.identification: It is a ground-dwelling bird with barred brown-and-buff plumage; displaying males raise neck feathers and inflate air sacs.
sections.habitat: It favors shortgrass prairie interspersed with shrubs, including sand-sagebrush and shinnery-oak grasslands.
sections.diet: Adults eat seeds and green plant parts, while chicks depend strongly on insects.
sections.behavior: Males gather at leks to display and attract females.
sections.reproduction: Females nest on the ground in grass cover, so suitable nesting vegetation near display and feeding areas matters.
sections.ecology: It is a close relative of the greater prairie-chicken, but generally uses shorter, shrub-mixed prairie.
sections.conservation: Maintaining extensive native shrub-grassland is central to its conservation.
